summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman, 15 weeks pregnant, was admitted for evaluation of left lower quadrant pain persisting for one week. With a history of endometriosis and chronic pelvic pain, she underwent a pelvic ultrasound and MRI of the abdomen and pelvis, both of which showed no acute abnormalities, ovarian torsion, or other structural causes. Her pain remained stable, and she had reassuring fetal monitoring throughout. Labs revealed mild leukocytosis and hypokalemia, which were managed supportively. Nausea was attributed to pregnancy and improved with antiemetics. After ruling out serious causes, she was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with her OB and a pain clinic, as the pain was likely related to her known endometriosis or normal pregnancy changes.
